name: Buon Ma Thuot food guide
summary: Buon Ma Thuot eats a red noodle bowl in the afternoon, rolls its own rice sheets one plate at a time, and keeps a highland table of bamboo rice, grilled yard chicken, bitter eggplant, and jar wine.
body: Start with coffee, black or with milk. At lunch, roll stacked rice sheets on Trần Nhật Duật or Lê Thánh Tông, one hot sheet to a plate. From about 15:00 or 16:00, the bún đỏ stalls set up on Le Hong Phong.

The other meal is Êđê and M’nông: sticky rice roasted in bamboo, yard chicken rubbed with lá ech, and a pull from the jar. Bitter eggplant runs through it, in soup, in salad, and pounded raw with chili, and at Tết the table runs from grilled meat to jar wine.
Da Lat’s charcoal pancakes belong to a different highland, and Nha Trang is the coast. Stay when the red bowl and the jar are the meal.
specialtiesLead: These are the plates people come to Buon Ma Thuot for, from the afternoon noodle stall to the longhouse jar.

sections.heading: Coffee
paragraphs: Coffee is the drink the town is known for. Order it black or with milk, in a plain room or a garden cafe.

spots.name: Coffee
spots.address: Nguyen Chi Thanh, Ako Dhong, and cafes through town
spots.note: Drunk black or with milk. At the head of Bà Triệu, one counter mixes the cup with a glass of ice cream.

sections.heading: The red bowl and the stacked sheets
paragraphs: Bún đỏ is the afternoon bowl, stacked rice sheets are the lunch you roll yourself, and nem nướng is grilled pork you wrap with herbs and green fruit.

spots.name: Bun do
spots.address: Le Hong Phong, and also Phan Boi Chau, Phan Dinh Giot, Le Duan, and the night market
spots.note: Thick red noodles in a pork-bone and crab broth, with crab cake, quail egg, fried shallot, and pork crackling. Stir in shrimp paste and chili, then the blanched greens.

spots.name: Stacked rice sheets
spots.address: Trần Nhật Duật and Lê Thánh Tông
spots.note: One ultra-thin hot sheet to a plate, rolled around grilled pork, sausage, pickles, and mango, and dipped in mắm nêm or a sweet-sour fish sauce. Stack the empty plates as you go.

spots.name: Grilled pork paste
spots.note: Minced pork grilled until the edges char, rolled in rice paper with herbs, green banana, and sour mango. The thick, warm dip is salty-sweet and nutty from peanuts.

sections.heading: Bamboo rice, chicken, and the jar
paragraphs: Jar wine, bamboo rice, and grilled chicken come as one Êđê and M’nông set, at Ko Tam in the city and at Buon Tri A in Buon Don. The river adds catfish from the Serepok.

spots.name: Bamboo sticky rice
spots.address: Ko Tam, Buon Ma Thuot, and Buon Tri A, Buon Don
spots.note: Sticky rice roasted in a fresh bamboo tube, soft and chewy and smelling of fresh bamboo. Split it and dip it in sesame salt, or eat it with grilled chicken.

spots.name: Grilled yard chicken
spots.address: Ko Tam, Buon Ma Thuot, and Buon Tri A, Buon Don
spots.note: Yard chicken rubbed with pounded lá ech and grilled until the skin turns golden without drying. The dip is salt pounded with lá ech, lá giang, culantro, scallion, and green chili.

spots.name: Jar wine
spots.address: Ako Dhong, and with the meal at Ko Tam or Buon Tri A
spots.note: Êđê wine of sticky rice and a galangal-and-leaf yeast, cloudy white, sweet, and fragrant. Everyone pulls from the same jar through long straws.

spots.name: Serepok catfish
spots.note: Catfish from the Serepok River, one of the foods that start in Buon Ma Thuot.

sections.heading: Bitter eggplant and forest greens
paragraphs: These are Êđê and M’nông plates: bitter eggplant cooked, pounded, and tossed, forest shoots on the grill, and river greens in soup. Bitter eggplant also goes into pots with fresh fish, dried shrimp, forest meat, or frog. Expect bitter and hot flavors, and plenty of rice.

spots.name: Pounded bamboo soup
spots.note: Lá bép, rattan shoots, bitter eggplant, and stream fish or meat, cooked in a bamboo tube and pounded with a chopstick. It finishes thick, bitter, hot, nutty, and fatty.

spots.name: Bitter-eggplant soup
spots.address: Stilt-house meals in Buon Don, Lak, or the city
spots.note: Bitter eggplant simmered with pounded dried fish and rice-washing water, or with beef offal and beef bung. Both are bitter and hot, and the offal pot is also sweet and fragrant.

spots.name: Bitter-eggplant salad
spots.note: Thin eggplant tossed with fried dried anchovy, culantro, and a garlic-chili fish sauce. Bitter, fragrant, salty, sweet, and hot.

spots.name: Pounded bitter eggplant
spots.note: Raw fruit pounded with salt, chili, lá é, and scallion. Very hot, and made for a lot of rice.

spots.name: Grilled rattan shoot
spots.note: A bitter, fragrant shoot from deep forest, grilled and dipped in salt pounded with xiêm chili.

spots.name: Cassava-leaf stir-fry
spots.note: Young cassava leaves and male papaya flowers stir-fried with steamed scad in pork fat over a very low flame. Bitter, fatty, and hot.

spots.name: Papaya with ant salt
spots.nameVi: Đu đủ giã muối kiến vàng
spots.address: Đường sách cà phê, at a highland tasting
spots.note: Pounded papaya with weaver-ant salt, served beside pounded bitter eggplant on a table guests called hot and bitter.

spots.name: Djam tang soup
spots.note: A fine river green from the Krông Ana, the Krông Knô, and the Serepok, cooked with stream fish. Sweet from the green and nutty from the fish.

spots.name: Sour djam tang
spots.note: The same river green, pickled sour, for dipping grilled meat and fish.

spots.name: Snakehead with ant eggs
spots.nameVi: Cá lóc canh chua trứng kiến
spots.address: Stilt-house meals in Buon Don, Lak, or the city
spots.note: A sour soup of snakehead fish with ant eggs, part of the forest meal with greens and bamboo rice.

spots.name: Stir-fried forest greens
spots.address: Stilt-house meals in Buon Don, Lak, or the city
spots.note: Forest greens stir-fried and eaten with the bitter-eggplant soup and the bamboo rice.

spots.name: Mnong flour soup
spots.note: A M’nông soup, served beside the Êđê bitter-eggplant soup among Dak Lak’s highland dishes.

sections.heading: Market snacks
paragraphs: Two market snacks and a tabletop pan: fried sticky-rice cakes on Phùng Chí Kiên, grilled honeycomb cake at the central market, and beef dipped in tamarind on Lê Thánh Tông.

spots.name: Fried sticky-rice cakes
spots.note: Sticky-rice cakes fried crisp and cut small, plain or filled with minced pork, wood-ear, and glass noodles. Eat them with salty-sweet soy or chili sauce.

spots.name: Grilled honeycomb cake
spots.note: A sweet cake grilled until the sugar scorches a little, so it tastes slightly burnt and bitter as well as sweet.

spots.name: Beef in tamarind
spots.note: Thin beef dipped into sweet-sour tamarind on a hot buttered pan. Dip a few slices at a time, or the beef turns tough.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: These plates belong to other Dak Lak districts: fish cake at Lak Lake, chicken rice in Ea Kar, mango and bamboo shoots in Ea Súp, and mì Quảng in Cư M’gar and Krông Pắc.

spots.name: Bronze-featherback cake
spots.note: Fish cake seasoned with only pepper and fish sauce and fried golden, crisp and naturally sweet, with a few dill stems.

spots.name: Ea Kar chicken rice
spots.note: Rice from Coffee Farm 721 cooked in the chicken liquor, tinted with turmeric, and fried in chicken fat until rich and crisp outside.

spots.name: Ea Sup mango
spots.note: The mango Ea Súp district is known for.

spots.name: Forest bamboo shoots
spots.note: Forest bamboo shoots, Ea Súp’s other specialty beside the mango.

spots.name: Chicken mi quang
spots.note: Mì Quảng with chicken, a highland bowl said to taste like nowhere else, not the Da Nang one.

spots.name: Frog mi quang
spots.note: Mì Quảng with frog, the second bowl those districts are known for.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Three places to sit down to the city’s food.

spots.name: Le Hong Phong bun do row
spots.nameVi: Phố bún đỏ Lê Hồng Phong
spots.note: A row of bún đỏ stalls sets up on this street from about 15:00 or 16:00.

spots.name: Central market
spots.note: Grilled honeycomb cake sells here in the afternoon.

spots.name: Ko Tam
spots.nameVi: Khu du lịch cộng đồng Kô Tam
spots.note: A community tourism area where jar wine, bamboo rice, and grilled chicken come to the table as one set.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Breakfast is a noodle bowl and a coffee. Hủ tiếu is common here, though not a local specialty.

spots.name: Pork-hock noodle soup
spots.note: Thin noodles with plenty of pork in a salty broth that is sweet from the meat, finished with herbs, lime, garlic, and chili.

spots.name: Hu tieu
spots.note: Seasoned saltier and less sweet than a southern bowl. Choose meat-and-bone, wonton, or Nam Vang.

seoTitle: Buon Ma Thuot food guide — bun do, bamboo rice, jar wine
seoDescription: Bun do on Le Hong Phong from about 15:00, stacked rice sheets, bamboo rice with grilled chicken and Ede jar wine, and bitter-eggplant plates.
